summary:
US tariff uncertainty is pushing fashion retailers to reassess Holiday 2026 supplier choices, inventory commitments and pricing plans.
Buyers are prioritising risk reduction over lowest-cost sourcing as landed-cost visibility weakens.
Suppliers with flexible production, shorter lead times, transparent costing and compliance strength stand to gain Holiday orders.

title: Solid monthly improvement in Vietnamese manufacturing health: PMI data
summary:
July data pointed to a strengthening of growth momentum in the Vietnamese manufacturing sector, with sharper increases recorded in output, new orders, exports and purchasing, while employment rose for the first time in five months, according to PMI data compiled by S&P Global. 
Input costs and output prices each rose at the slowest rates in 10 months. 
Supply-chain delays were also less pronounced.

title: Indonesia’s cotton spindles fell 59% as China orders jumped 136%
summary:
China imported $62.45 million of Indonesian cotton yarn in January-April 2026, up 135.6 per cent year on year, giving underused mills a demand boost.
The rebound is concentrated in HS 5205 and remains far below 2021 trade levels, limiting its value as a recovery signal.
Indonesia’s spindle base has reportedly shrunk to 4.5-5 million, while cotton-mill utilisation is still only 40-50 per cent.

title: ICE cotton climbs on institutional buying, limited rainfall
summary:
ICE cotton extended gains for a third straight session, supported by strong export demand, continued Chinese reserve buying, tightening certified stocks and rising open interest.
US crop conditions weakened slightly but remained above the long-term average.
Market attention is now on whether the December contract can break the key 82.96-cent resistance level.

title: Asian VSF price floor faces supply-driven upside risk
summary:
Asian VSF prices were unchanged in India, Pakistan and China in the week ended July 31, with TexPro-tracked grades showing 0.00 per cent intra-week movement.
Firm pulp costs, Chinese maintenance and administered or import-linked pricing kept spot offers steady despite weak spinning demand.
Lenzing’s restructuring adds medium-term MMCF supply risk for sourcing teams.

title: Can China’s foreign exchange reforms strengthen supply chains?
summary:
China plans to further open foreign exchange rules in the second half of 2026, with nationwide facilitation for cross-border trade receipts and payments.
The measures cover cross-border e-commerce, service-trade settlement and intermediate goods trade, key areas for sourcing and supply chains.
Multinationals will see wider centralised cross-border fund operations.

title: Europe powered 67% of Egypt’s apparel export growth
summary:
Egypt’s apparel exports rose 15 per cent to $1.775 billion in H1 2026, with Europe delivering about 67 per cent of the net gain.
Europe and the US supplied 82.3 per cent of shipments, exposing exporters to market and product concentration.
TexPro data point to woven demand in Europe, knitted growth in the US, and higher EU compliance pressure from July 19, 2026.

title: Japan's Yonex begins renewable solar power use at Niigata factory
summary:
Yonex has begun using renewable solar energy at its Niigata Factory Nagaoka through an on-site PPA.  The 896.72 kW system is expected to generate about 850,000 kWh annually and cut CO₂ emissions by around 295 tons. 
The initiative supports Yonex’s Carbon Neutrality goals and expands its use of renewable energy across manufacturing sites.

title: India’s Raymond Lifestyle’s Q1 earnings grow 11%; garmenting jumps 50%
summary:
Raymond Lifestyle has reported a stable Q1 FY27, with total income rising 6 per cent YoY to ₹1,560 crore (~$163.7 million) and EBITDA up 11 per cent to ₹135 crore (~$14.17 million). 
Strong garmenting growth, driven by export demand and trade tailwinds, offset softer textile performance. 
The company also strengthened its balance sheet, ending the quarter with a net cash position.

title: Bangladesh can unlock $5 bn apparel exports with plastic recycling
summary:
Bangladesh could add $4-5 billion in apparel exports by scaling plastic-to-textile recycling, BUILD has estimated. 
The push targets lower reliance on imported man-made fibres and alignment with European Union's circularity requirements. 
Policy proposals include a circular economy policy, better collection, traceability, recycled PET standards and certification.

title: Albania’s apparel exports grow 36% in Jan-April, momentum continues
summary:
Albania’s apparel exports rose 36.8 per cent year on year to $193.19 million in January-April 2026, TexPro data showed.
Nearshoring demand from European fashion buyers lifted CMT-led orders as brands sought shorter lead times and sourcing flexibility.
Imports more than doubled to $156.25 million, indicating higher inward processing for re-export rather than domestic demand.

title: Turkiye’s apparel exports decline to $7.7 bn in H1, but surge in June
summary:
Turkiye’s apparel exports fell 1.78 per cent year on year to $7.794 billion in January-June 2026, with knitted and woven categories both lower.
June shipments rebounded 14.75 per cent to $1.330 billion, the strongest monthly growth so far in 2026.
Turkiye's apparel exports have been on a downward trajectory over the past three years.

title: South Korea’s apparel imports inches up to $5.6 billion in H1, 2026
summary:
South Korea’s apparel imports rose 2.27 per cent to $5.658 billion in January-June 2026, with June shipments up 4.54 per cent year on year. 
Knitted apparel imports grew faster than non-knitted categories, signalling uneven sourcing demand across garment types. 
Fabric and filament exports weakened in the first half, affecting South Korea’s textile trade mix.

title: Canada Goose reports higher Q1 sales, improved margins
summary:
Canada Goose’s Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21 per cent to C$84.8 million (~$60.4 million); losses narrowed and gross margin reached 66.1 per cent. 
DTC sales grew 37 per cent on higher store and e-commerce traffic and conversions; wholesale fell 12 per cent as partner demand softened. 
The brand kept FY27 guidance at C$1.4–1.5 billion (~$997.5 million–$1.07 billion) and plans four to six DTC stores.

title: US’ Columbia Sportswear returns to profit in Q2, lifts FY26 outlook
summary:
American manufacturer and distributor Columbia Sportswear Company has returned to profitability in Q2 FY26 as net sales rose 2 per cent to $614.4 million, supported by international growth and a $78 million IEEPA tariff refund. 
The company raised its FY26 profit and EPS guidance, while maintaining its sales outlook despite softer US demand and ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty.

title: Canada's Gildan Activewear's Q1 revenue surges 64% on HanesBrands deal
summary:
Gildan Activewear Inc, a Canadian apparel manufacturer, posted record first-quarter net sales of $1.17 billion, rising 63.8 per cent YoY, driven by the full consolidation of HanesBrands. 
Despite the revenue jump, Gildan reported a net loss of $55.1 million from continuing operations and an operating margin of negative 0.1 per cent. 
Adjusted operating margin reached 14.3 per cent.
